blocks.text: 1. Decoder-Only Models
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785446022317-197342461.png

Encoder-Only Models, the previous topic, dropped the decoder entirely for understanding-focused tasks. Decoder-Only Models are the opposite architectural family, dropping the encoder instead, explored throughout this topic.

They use genuinely just the decoder half already covered, without a genuinely separate encoder at all, a genuinely important, contrasting architectural family covered throughout the rest of this topic.
2. Recapping The Opposite Simplification
This connects back to Encoder-Only Models, already covered in its own topic. That earlier topic genuinely dropped the decoder; this topic genuinely does the exact opposite.
It drops the encoder instead, keeping just the decoder, a genuinely direct, mirrored simplification of the exact same overall Transformer architecture already covered throughout the previous module.
3. No Cross-Attention Needed
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785446022318-869568160.png

This connects back to Cross-Attention to the encoder, already covered in The Decoder. Without a genuinely separate encoder at all, already covered in this topic, there is genuinely no encoder output to attend to.

Decoder-Only Models genuinely drop Cross-Attention entirely, keeping just Self-Attention, a genuinely direct structural consequence of the encoder's own absence already covered in the previous section.

blocks.text: 4. Causal Masking Remains
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785446022319-199542984.png
This connects back to Causal Masking, already covered in its own topic. Decoder-Only Models genuinely still need Causal Masking, exactly as already covered there.
This holds since they genuinely still generate output one position at a time, one word after another, exactly the sequential constraint already covered as necessary for any genuine decoder.
5. A Single, Unified Input Stream
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785446022319-431249918.png

A genuinely important, distinctive structural simplification connects back to the encoder output feeds into the decoder, already covered in The Encoder. There is genuinely only one single input stream, processed and generated entirely within one unified structure.

This genuinely eliminates the two-stream handoff already covered there entirely, making Decoder-Only Models genuinely structurally simpler than the full encoder-decoder Transformer already covered throughout the previous module.
6. The Next-Token Prediction Task
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785446022320-52476086.png

This connects back to sequential word generation, already covered in Image Captioning. Decoder-Only Models genuinely train by predicting the genuinely next token, given everything genuinely before it.
This is a genuinely simple, elegant training objective explored further throughout the rest of this course, requiring genuinely no separate labels beyond the text itself.

10. Worked Example

The example below directly demonstrates a Decoder-Only Model's own pipeline, generating text one token at a time using causal Self-Attention alone, illustrating the concepts already covered throughout this topic.

code.content:
import numpy as np

rng = np.random.RandomState(42)
hidden_size = 8
vocab_size = 6

def softmax(x):
    exp_x = np.exp(x - np.max(x, axis=-1, keepdims=True))
    return exp_x / exp_x.sum(axis=-1, keepdims=True)

def decoder_only_layer(x, rng):
    # already covered as causal masking remains in this topic
    seq_len = x.shape[0]
    causal_mask = np.triu(np.ones((seq_len, seq_len)), k=1).astype(bool)
    W_q, W_k, W_v = [rng.normal(size=(hidden_size, hidden_size)) * 0.1 for _ in range(3)]
    q, k, v = x @ W_q.T, x @ W_k.T, x @ W_v.T
    scores = q @ k.T / np.sqrt(hidden_size)
    scores[causal_mask] = -np.inf
    x = x + softmax(scores) @ v  # already covered as no Cross-Attention needed in this topic
    x = x + np.tanh(x @ (rng.normal(size=(hidden_size, hidden_size)) * 0.1))
    return x

generated_tokens = rng.normal(size=(1, hidden_size))  # a genuinely simplified starting token

for step in range(4):  # already covered as the next-token prediction task in this topic
    hidden_representation = decoder_only_layer(generated_tokens, rng)
    next_token = hidden_representation[-1:] + rng.normal(scale=0.1, size=(1, hidden_size))
    generated_tokens = np.concatenate([generated_tokens, next_token], axis=0)
    print(f"Step {step + 1}: generated sequence length = {generated_tokens.shape[0]}")

print("\nThis entire process used genuinely only one single, unified input stream, already covered in this topic")

blocks.text: 11. Key Takeaways

items: Decoder-Only Models use just the decoder half of the Transformer, dropping the encoder entirely.
Without a separate encoder, they drop Cross-Attention entirely, keeping just Self-Attention.
They still need Causal Masking, since they still generate output one position at a time.
There is only one single, unified input stream, eliminating the two-stream handoff.
They train by predicting the next token, given everything before it.
GPT stands as the single most influential decoder-only model, covered in the very next topic.
This simplified, single-stream design scales remarkably well to enormous sizes.
They suit open-ended text generation tasks well.
Next up: Encoder-Decoder Models, keeping both halves for tasks needing both understanding and generation.
